title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and driving forces of forest NPP in Northeast China based on National Forest Inventory Data
content:
Abstract
Understanding spatiotemporal dynamic changes in forest Net Primary Productivity (NPP) and their drivers is essential for mitigating climate change and adaptive forest management. However, the factors driving the upward and downward trends in NPP remain unclear, especially at large scales. The aims of this study were to quantify spatiotemporal variations in NPP, examine the NPP characteristics of different forest types, and identify the dominant factors affecting NPP change trends (increase or decrease) from 2004 to 2024 in Jilin Province, Northeast China. We estimated and analyzed the temporal and spatial variation patterns of NPP via the Carnegie–Ames–Stanford A pproach model, Theil–Sen median trend analysis, and the Mann–Kendall test. The NPP prediction model was developed by combining data from 3154 permanent sample plots with climate, soil, and stand data. The dominant factors affecting NPP change were explored by applying a multivariable screening method and developing random forest models. The results revealed that: (i) the mean NPP of forests was 734.42 g C/m2 in Jilin Province with an increased trend from 2004 to 2024. Spatially, NPP exhibited a distribution pattern with high values in the southwest and low in the northeast. (ii) Among the 12 forest types in Jilin Province, Mongolian oak forest had the highest NPP, whereas poplar (Populus L.) forest had the lowest. (3) For areas with increasing NPP, the key factors and importance values were snowfall (24.89), soil pH (20.78%), Hargreaves climatic moisture deficit (19.26), annual range of temperature (15.01), forest type (11.62%), and stand age (8.44%). In NPP decreasing areas, organic carbon stock (28.91%), total nitrogen (23.96), extreme maximum temperature (16.82%), forest type (12.15%), stand age (9.95%), and mean warmest month temperature (8.21%) were identified as key drivers. The findings could provide a theoretical foundation for enhancing forest productivity and formulating targeted management strategies.
